fields.h1: Build a Scored Quiz That Weights Questions and Sets a Pass Mark
fields.hero_description: Get a scored quiz that weights each question and shows a result screen for each score band.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Scored Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A scored quiz adds up the points from each answer and turns the total into a result. Emergent builds both from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A point value on every question

Tell Emergent which questions matter more, such as 2 points for each safety question and 1 for the rest. The top score and the pass mark update whenever a weight changes.
fields.feature_2:
A result screen for each band

Split the score range into bands, such as 0 to 9, 10 to 15, and 16 to 20, and give each one its own title and message. Players see theirs right after the last answer.
fields.feature_3:
Partial credit where it is fair

Select-all questions can earn a point for each correct pick instead of all or nothing. Decide whether a wrong pick costs a point; the app never scores a question below 0.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when someone misses the mark

Pick a pass mark, and the app emails the trainer or posts to a Slack channel with the name of each person who scored under it. Reminders follow until the retake is done.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer kept with its points

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the points it earned. Sort by question to find the one that costs players the most, then rewrite it before round 2.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Run the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a scored quiz?

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a scored quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: Searchers for a scored quiz want to know how the points turn into a result: what each question is worth, where the pass mark sits, and what each score band shows. This page lets them score 8 quiz questions by hand on the page, then shows four scored quizzes a hotel, a design studio, a wine school, and a taproom run as their own app, each with its own point rule, and a seven-step method for weighting, banding, and testing the scoring before launch.
tab_stories: Grayhaven Hotels gives 48 new front desk hires a 15-question training quiz where the 5 fire evacuation questions are worth 2 points each, so the top score is 20 and the pass mark is 16; 9 fall short and training lead Gethin Strakosch gets an email naming them before Friday's retake.

Lumbard Studio puts a 10-question website readiness quiz on its site, each answer worth 0 to 10 points; 412 visitors finished it in September, and the 58 who scored 70 or more posted to Slack for Renske Junot to call.

Vinterra Wine School runs a 25-question certificate exam worth 35 points, with 5 select-all questions that give a point per correct pick; 51 of 64 students reach the 28-point pass mark, 7 of them only because of partial credit.

Hopstead Brewing runs trivia night as 6 rounds of 8 questions with the last round worth double, for 56 points in all; the leaderboard on the bar TV updates after each round, and Table Nine wins 14 teams with 47 points.
